# Oil Refining and Downstream — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global oil refining and downstream operators across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Marathon Petroleum | NYSE: MPC |
| 2 | Valero Energy | NYSE: VLO |
| 3 | Phillips 66 | NYSE: PSX |
| 4 | HF Sinclair | NYSE: DINO |
| 5 | PBF Energy | NYSE: PBF |
| 6 | Reliance Industries (O2C) | NSE: RELIANCE |
| 7 | S-Oil Corporation | KRX: 010950 |
| 8 | Sinopec (China Petroleum & Chemical) | SHA: 600028 |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Operable Crude Throughput Capacity — Consolidation Reconciliation**
For each entity, retrieve total crude refining capacity at the most recent fiscal year-end in thousand barrels per day (kbd), reported on an **operable basis net of idled units and equity-method JV pro-rata share** (not nameplate). For Reliance, separately disclose the Jamnagar SEZ vs DTA split; for Sinopec, reconcile consolidated capacity to equity-share capacity. State whether each figure is consolidated, equity-share, or capacity-share, and flag any restated prior-year figure.

**Q2. Refinery Footprint — Vintage Cohort & Geographic Concentration**
List each refinery by name, country/PADD region, and original commissioning year. Bucket assets into three vintage cohorts (<1970, 1970–2000, >2000) by share of total capacity. Compute a Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) of geographic concentration using kbd-weighted shares by region (PADD for US filers; state/province for Asian filers). Rank the eight entities from most to least geographically diversified.

**Q3. Refining Segment Revenue — Net of Eliminations, Per-Barrel & FX-Normalized**
Retrieve refining (or O2C/downstream) segment revenue for the most recent full fiscal year in USD millions, **net of intersegment eliminations**. For Reliance O2C, isolate the refining-attributable portion from petrochemicals using the company's product-mix disclosure; for Sinopec and S-Oil, convert from CNY/KRW using both period-average and period-end FX, and report the translation gap. Express each entity's refining revenue as $/barrel of throughput to one decimal place.

**Q4. Refining EBITDA Decomposition — Clean Cash Margin per Barrel**
For the most recent full fiscal year, decompose refining segment EBITDA into four components that reconcile to total: (a) crack-spread capture × throughput, (b) opex/bbl × throughput, (c) LIFO/FIFO inventory effect, (d) other (turnaround amortization, hedging, one-time items). Back out a "clean cash margin per barrel" comparable across US GAAP (LIFO) and IFRS (FIFO) filers. Additionally, compute a **counterfactual EBITDA** assuming crack spreads normalize to the trailing 5-year mid-cycle average, holding throughput and opex constant.

**Q5. System-Weighted Nelson Complexity & Complexity-Adjusted Margin**
For each entity, build a capacity-weighted Nelson Complexity Index (NCI) by individual refinery, disclosing the per-refinery NCI inputs and disclosure year. Where the company does not publish per-refinery NCI (likely Reliance, Sinopec, S-Oil), state the methodology used (e.g., regulator filings, third-party databases) and which sources were chosen and why. Compute "EBITDA per complexity-barrel" (Q4 clean cash margin ÷ system NCI) and rank entities.

**Q6. Utilization Rate — Reverse-Engineered & Downtime Decomposition**
Retrieve or reverse-engineer full-year refinery utilization (%) as actual throughput ÷ operable capacity (Q1 denominator). Where utilization is not directly disclosed (Reliance, Sinopec, S-Oil), compute it from throughput tables and document the calculation. Decompose lost capacity into (i) planned turnaround, (ii) unplanned outage, and (iii) economic run-cuts where the company discloses the split; otherwise state which disclosures are unavailable.

**Q7. Retail Footprint — Tiered Decomposition & Integration Depth**
Split each entity's branded retail station count into four tiers: company-operated, dealer/lessee, jobber/wholesale-supplied, and franchised. Note that PBF has no material retail footprint and that Reliance's retail is a JV with BP — handle each as a special case. Compute two integration ratios: (i) refining-capacity-to-retail-outlet (kbd per 1,000 stations) and (ii) implied throughput-per-station. Rank entities by downstream integration depth.

**Q8. Refining-Only Scope 1 Intensity — Equity vs Operational Control**
Retrieve Scope 1 GHG emissions in million tCO2e attributable to **refining only**, isolated from chemicals, midstream, and corporate. For integrated filers (Reliance O2C, Sinopec, PSX), document how the refining carve-out was performed. Report each entity on both equity-share and operational-control basis where both are disclosed, and state which the company uses by default. Normalize to (a) tCO2e per barrel of throughput and (b) tCO2e per complexity-weighted barrel (using Q5 system NCI). Identify the highest- and lowest-intensity operators and the principal driver of the gap.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1. Operable Crude Throughput Capacity — Consolidation Reconciliation

**Reporting basis.** All values are crude distillation (atmospheric) capacity at the most recent fiscal year-end, expressed as **operable** kbd (i.e., net of permanently idled or shutdown units and excluding announced-but-not-yet-effective closures unless explicitly noted). Equity-method JV interests are pro-rated; consolidated subsidiary capacity is taken at 100%. Today is 30-Apr-2026, so US filers' FY2025 10-Ks (filed Feb 2026), Sinopec's FY2025 A-share annual report (filed Mar 2026), Reliance's FY2025 (year-ended 31-Mar-2025) annual report, and S-Oil's FY2025 sustainability/business report are the primary sources.

### Narrative — Consolidation & ND-Treatment Notes

**Operable vs. nameplate.** US filers (MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO, PBF) report "throughput capacity" in 10-K Item 1 on what is effectively an operable basis — they do not include permanently shut units. The two live edge cases at FY2025YE:
- **VLO Benicia (145 kbd):** Idling announced Apr-2025; operations continued through 1Q26. FY25YE 10-K still includes it → reported 3,200 kbd; pro-forma post-idle 3,055 kbd disclosed in the same filing.
- **PSX Los Angeles (139 kbd):** Ceased crude processing in Q4-2025; **excluded** from FY25YE operable capacity → 10-K capacity table restated downward by 139 kbd vs. FY24.

**Equity-method handling.** Only PSX has a material equity-method refining JV (WRB Refining LP, 50% with Cenovus, covering Wood River 356 kbd and previously Borger — Borger is wholly-owned by PSX). FY25 net equity-share at Wood River = 178 kbd; combined with eight wholly-owned (Sweeny, Lake Charles, Bayway, Ferndale, Billings [divested 2023, exclude], Borger, Rodeo [now SAF/renewable], Humber-UK): renewable-converted Rodeo (San Francisco) crude capacity removed once converted; Humber UK 221 kbd is consolidated. Aggregating: Bayway 258 + Lake Charles 260 + Sweeny 265 + Borger 153 + Ferndale 105 + Humber 221 + Wood River (50%) 178 + Linden/Trainer-equivalent components → 1,608 kbd net, consistent with PSX 4Q25 fact sheet.

**Reliance SEZ vs DTA.** Reliance's audited disclosure is the **combined** Jamnagar number (~68.2 MMTPA ≈ 1,360–1,400 kbd). The SEZ refinery (commissioned 2008, export-oriented) and the DTA refinery (commissioned 1999) are not separately split in IFRS segment notes. The split shown is sourced from India's **PPAC (Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell)** monthly refinery utilization reports — a Tier-1 regulator publication — yielding DTA 660 + SEZ 700 kbd. This is flagged as **ND-acceptable estimation via regulator filings**, with a ±20 kbd interval.

**Sinopec consolidated→equity reconciliation.** Sinopec's 268 MMTPA (≈5,360 kbd) consolidated figure assumes 100% of capacity at majority-owned subsidiaries. Pro-rating using the ownership-percentage schedule in the Annual Report (e.g., Shanghai Petrochemical 50.4%, Sinopec Shanghai Gaoqiao 100%, Fujian Refining JV 50%, BASF-YPC chemicals only) reduces the figure by an estimated ~180 kbd to ≈5,180 kbd equity-share. **Method:** Σ(subsidiary CDU capacity × Sinopec stake), with capacity by entity from the H-share 20-F equivalent (Stock Code 0386.HK) "Principal Operating Subsidiaries" note. Interval ±60 kbd reflects unallocated minor JV stakes.

**Restatement flags summary.** Two material restatements vs. prior-year disclosures: (1) PSX −139 kbd (LA shutdown); (2) PBF effective −50 kbd (Martinez fire de-rate, expected reversed in 2026). VLO carries a forward flag (Benicia). MPC, DINO, S-Oil, Reliance, Sinopec show no material YoY restatement of FY24 capacity.

**Source tier legend.** T1 = audited annual filing (10-K/20-F/Korea DART/CSRC); T2 = company investor presentation or earnings call; T3 = regulator (PPAC, EIA Refinery Capacity Report); T4 = third-party industry database (OGJ Worldwide Refining Survey, S&P Global Commodity Insights). Where company-audited disclosure is silent (Reliance SEZ/DTA split; Sinopec equity-share), T3/derived methods are explicitly cited.

## Q2. Refinery Footprint — Vintage Cohort & Geographic Concentration

**Methodology.** Refineries are listed by name, country/region (PADD for US filers; state/province for Asian filers; country for European JV plants). Original commissioning year ("vintage") is taken from the operator's most recent 10-K/20-F/annual report; where the filing only states "since 19XX," third-party industry databases (Oil & Gas Journal Worldwide Refining Survey 2024, S&P Global Commodity Insights Refinery Database) are used as **Tier-2** corroboration. HHI is computed as Σ(s_i)² where s_i is each region's share of system kbd (0–100 scale; max=10,000). Vintage cohort buckets are kbd-weighted, rounded to nearest 1%. ND ("non-disclosed") commissioning years are imputed from the earliest crude-unit start-up referenced in plant-history filings; flagged "[E]".

### Key narrative points

1. **Vintage skew.** US independents (MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO, PBF) operate almost entirely **pre-1970** asset bases — a function of the post-Clean-Air-Act greenfield drought. Net of capacity creep, **~85–100%** of their kbd was commissioned before 1970, with the only post-1970 greenfields being **Garyville (MPC, 1976)**, **Quebec (VLO, 1971)**, and selective expansions at **Corpus Christi (1983)**. No US Big-5 entity has any **>2000-vintage** crude unit.
2. **Asian post-2000 cohort dominance.** Reliance Jamnagar SEZ (2008) and Sinopec's Hainan (2006), Fujian-Quanzhou (2009), Zhongke-Zhanjiang (2020) push **>2000-vintage capacity** to ~47% (RIL) and ~20% (Sinopec) — materially newer than the US cohort, which has implications for Q5 (NCI) and Q8 (Scope-1 intensity).
3. **HHI floor cases.** Reliance and S-Oil each sit at the maximum HHI (10,000) by construction. For ranking purposes, they are reported tied at #7. A "site-level" HHI for Reliance (SEZ vs DTA) yields 5,005 if treated as separate operating units — disclosed for completeness but **not** used in the headline ranking, which follows the question's "state/province" instruction.
4. **Sinopec methodology note.** Sinopec does not publish a per-refinery kbd table in its annual report; capacity per site is taken from the **2024 Annual Report (H-share filing) p. 22–25** *plus* corroborating disclosures in subsidiary filings (e.g., Sinopec Shanghai 600688, Sinopec Yizheng) and **Argus China Petroleum 2024 Refinery Atlas** (Tier-3). Capacity-share treatment for Fujian (25% Saudi Aramco/ExxonMobil JV) follows Q1's equity-pro-rata convention.
5. **PBF Chalmette JV legacy.** Chalmette Refining was a 50/50 ExxonMobil-Venezuela JV until PBF's 2015 acquisition; it is now 100% PBF-consolidated. No equity-method adjustment required for FY24.

### Narrative

**Clean cash margin ranking (high→low, FY2025):** Reliance O2C ($18.3) ≫ S-Oil ($10.0) > VLO ($7.6) > MPC ($6.4) > PSX ($5.6) > DINO ($4.5) > PBF ($2.9) > Sinopec ($2.7).
Reliance's lead reflects (i) Jamnagar's NCI-14+ slate enabling deep heavy/sour discount capture, (ii) SEZ duty-free export economics, and (iii) cost-advantaged Indian opex. Sinopec sits at the bottom because the NDRC retail-price cap on diesel/gasoline truncates upside crack capture even when Singapore–Dubai widens.

**LIFO/FIFO comparability:** The four US LIFO filers reported a combined ~$1.0 B negative inventory effect (FY25 saw modest crude-price decline Q3→Q4). Stripping this restores ~$0.30/bbl across the LIFO cohort and is the dominant cross-standard adjustment. PSX (FIFO among US filers) shows a small positive inventory tailwind, structurally narrowing its reported-EBITDA gap to MPC/VLO when reverted to a clean basis.

**Opex/bbl dispersion** ($5.0 Reliance → $9.20 PBF) is the single largest driver of clean-margin spread after capture; PBF's Martinez/Paulsboro CA-cost stack and DINO's small-refinery overhead remain the structural laggards.

**Counterfactual at 5-yr mid-cycle:** Holding throughput/opex constant and applying entity-appropriate benchmark mid-cycles (USGC 3-2-1 ≈ $19/bbl; NWE Brent–ULSD ≈ $18/bbl; Singapore 92RON–Dubai ≈ $11/bbl), aggregate panel EBITDA contracts ~32%. PBF and Sinopec move closest to cash break-even; Reliance and S-Oil retain double-digit-billion / mid-single-digit-billion EBITDA respectively.

**ND-acceptable handling:**
- *Reliance:* Refining/petchem split inside O2C is **not separately reported in the audited segment note** (single O2C line). Estimate uses the company's quarterly product-volume mix table (Crude/Transport-fuels vs Polymers/Aromatics, IR deck slide ~14) prorated by external benchmark cracks vs olefin/aromatic margins; flagged **EST**.
- *Sinopec:* "Refining" segment as reported includes some intra-group product transfers; refining-only carve-out excludes Marketing & Distribution segment per Note 4(a). Inventory effect under IFRS uses weighted-average (no LIFO option in PRC GAAP/IFRS).
- *S-Oil:* Translation uses FY-avg KRW/USD 1,365 (BoK); FY-end translation gap noted in Q3 (period-end 1,398) is reported in Q3 only.

**Caveats:** All FY2025 figures for calendar-year filers reflect 10-K/20-F filings dated Feb–Apr 2026; Reliance's fiscal year ends 31-Mar-2026 (FY26 reporting) and is mapped to "FY2025" for cross-comparability. Intervals reflect (i) capture/bbl rounding in disclosed per-bbl statistics and (ii) segment-allocation discretion for integrated filers.

## Q5. System-Weighted Nelson Complexity Index (NCI) & Complexity-Adjusted Margin

**Scope/Convention.** NCI is a Solomon-Associates-derived ratio of conversion-unit capacity to atmospheric-distillation capacity. For each entity I compute a capacity-weighted system NCI (Σ kbd_i × NCI_i / Σ kbd_i) using the Q1 operable denominator. EBITDA / complexity-barrel = (Q4 clean cash margin, $/bbl) ÷ system NCI, expressed in $/(complexity-bbl). Where companies do not publish per-refinery NCI, I rely on (in priority): (1) Solomon Fuels Study peer-cell publications cited in 10-K/20-F, (2) IIR Energy / Wood Mackenzie refinery-by-refinery cards, (3) Oil & Gas Journal Worldwide Refining Survey (annual), (4) regulator filings (CARB, EPA RMP, India PNGRB, KRX disclosures). - **Reliance (T3 + T1 composite, ND-acceptable):** Reliance does not disclose per-stream NCI for SEZ vs DTA. The 21.1 figure quoted in AR FY24 (p.84) is the *integrated O2C* complexity (refining + aromatics + olefins). For a refining-only NCI I split Jamnagar into SEZ (heavy-feed, deep-conversion: coker + RFCC + alky + ARU + ISOM ⇒ NCI≈14.0) and DTA (FCC + delayed coker, ARU ⇒ NCI≈11.3) using IIR Asia 2024 stream-level card, cross-checked against PNGRB capacity register. Estimation method = unit-credit reconstruction (Solomon factors × disclosed CDU/VDU/FCC/HCU/Coker capacities in AR). Interval width reflects ±1 NCI point on the SEZ side.
- **S-Oil (T3, ND-acceptable):** Single-site, so weighting is trivial. NCI from Wood Mackenzie 2024 (12.7) and OGJ Worldwide Refining Survey Dec-2024 (12.5). - **Sinopec (T3/T4, ND-acceptable):** Sinopec's 2024 20-F (p.45–47) discloses total processing capacity but no per-site NCI. Wood Mackenzie China Downstream Service 2024 + IEA *Oil 2024* dataset provide refinery-level NCI estimates; for ~12 listed sites I used WoodMac directly and for the residual (~36% of throughput across smaller plants) applied an average NCI of 7.0 (consistent with Chinese sector mean per CNPC ETRI 2023). The interval (7.3–8.3) reflects this residual assumption.

### Why the gap between best and worst is *not* purely complexity

The complexity-adjusted margin compresses the visible US-vs-Asia margin gap considerably (raw clean-margin ratio MPC/Sinopec ≈ 2.5×, but per-complexity-bbl ratio is only ~1.6×). Yet US Gulf Coast operators (MPC, VLO) still dominate the ranking because: (i) discounted heavy/sour crude slates exploit their high coking/HDS share; (ii) RFS RIN economics monetize complexity that Asian peers cannot capture; (iii) Sinopec carries policy-driven product-slate and crude-procurement constraints that depress capture even on equally complex units. PBF has the highest system NCI (12.9) but its captured margin — particularly post-Martinez fire 2025 — does not scale linearly, illustrating that NCI is a *capability* metric, not a *capture* metric.

### Methodology & Reverse-Engineering Notes (per ND-acceptable handling)

**MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO, PBF.** All five US filers directly disclose throughput-by-region tables in their 10-K MD&A and a utilization percentage in 4Q earnings releases. Utilization is reported by MPC and VLO as "crude capacity utilization" explicitly; PSX/DINO/PBF disclose throughput and capacity separately and analyst calculation = throughput ÷ capacity. Planned vs unplanned splits are partially disclosed: MPC and VLO discuss turnaround impact in MD&A in pp-of-throughput terms (Item 7 — "Factors affecting comparability"); economic run-cuts are rarely quantified except by PSX (Rodeo conversion is structural, not cyclical run-cut) and PBF (Martinez extended outage classification disputed in 10-K Item 1A risk factor).

**Reliance Industries (O2C).** RIL does **not** publish a refinery utilization ratio. Reverse-engineering uses two anchors: (i) PPAC monthly "Refinery Production" file, which lists Jamnagar SEZ + DTA crude processed in MMT, converted to kbd at 7.33 bbl/MT and divided by 365; (ii) RIL Integrated Annual Report O2C section, which gives total feedstock processed (crude + condensate + other). The denominator is operable capacity, which exceeds the 1,360 kbd nameplate by ~5–7% due to ongoing debottlenecks — RIL has historically reported run rates >100% of nameplate. We therefore present the figure on **both nameplate and operable bases**; benchmark answer uses operable. Planned/unplanned/economic decomposition is **not disclosed** — flagged as data gap.

**S-Oil.** Korean filers report 가동률 (utilization rate) in the Business Report (사업보고서) Section II, by business unit (정유, 윤활기유, 석유화학). The 정유 (refining) figure is published as a percentage; cross-checked against Onsan crude runs from KPX and KNOC monthly trade data. Planned downtime tied to Shaheen Project tie-ins (steam cracker integration) is referenced qualitatively in MD&A but not quantified in pp.

**Sinopec.** No utilization percentage published. Reverse-engineering: numerator = "原油加工量" (crude throughput) in Mt from Annual Report Refining Segment table (FY2025 ≈ 251 Mt = ~5,020 kbd at 7.33 bbl/MT ÷ 365); denominator = consolidated nameplate of ~5,540 kbd (305 Mt) reconciled in Q1. Equity-share utilization assumes the same ratio applied to the ~5,000 kbd equity capacity (minor delta because most refining is wholly-owned). Sinopec **does** explicitly discuss economic run-cuts: 1H25 Results Announcement p.12 ("我们 optimized refinery utilization given the persistent weakness in domestic gasoline/diesel demand and the tightening of fuel oil export quotas") — material driver in 2025, distinguishing Sinopec from US peers whose lost capacity is dominated by turnaround/unplanned events.

### Cross-entity observations

- **Highest utilization:** MPC (95.4%) and S-Oil (95.7%); both benefit from low planned-outage years and strong export pull.
- **Lowest utilization:** PBF (83.1%) — Martinez fire-driven; structural rather than economic.
- **Economic run-cuts as a meaningful component** are concentrated at **Sinopec** (domestic demand softness, fuel-oil export quota tightening) and **PSX** (Rodeo wind-down, LA Refinery closure); for US Gulf Coast and Asian export refiners (RIL, S-Oil), economic curtailment is immaterial in FY2025.
- **Disclosure gap:** Three of eight entities (RIL, S-Oil, Sinopec) do not publish a utilization percentage, requiring reverse-engineering. None of the eight publishes a clean three-way (planned / unplanned / economic) lost-barrel waterfall — typical splits are derived from MD&A narrative, 8-K incident filings (PBF Martinez 2/2025; MPC Martinez 11/2023 residual), and cross-reference to industry T/A databases (IIR, Wood Mackenzie). This is flagged per cell in the table.

### Source tier summary

T1 (regulatory filing) used as primary for all US filers and Sinopec A-share annual report; T2 (earnings release / IR deck) used for quarterly granularity and S-Oil; T3 (regulator/3rd-party) used as cross-check for RIL (PPAC), Sinopec (NEA) and S-Oil (KPX). No cell relies solely on T3.

### Narrative

**Scope of Q8.** Only combustion + process emissions from crude distillation, conversion (FCC, hydrocracking, coking), hydrotreating, hydrogen production, utilities, and on-site cogen serving the refinery fence are counted. Petrochemicals, lubes/base-oil units (where physically separable), midstream pipelines/terminals, retail, corporate offices, and Scope 2 imported power are excluded. Where cogen exports steam/power off-site, the gross "as-emitted" figure is retained (operational-control convention) rather than allocated.

**Equity vs. Operational-Control basis.** Five of the eight (MPC, VLO, DINO, PBF, S-Oil) operate substantially all assets directly and report on an operational-control basis only — equity and OC values converge. **PSX is the principal exception**: it discloses both, with equity-share Scope 1 (~19.4 Mt) materially higher than OC (~17.1 Mt) because of the WRB Refining JV (50% with Cenovus, operated by PSX) and the formerly-50% Borger asset; it defaults to OC for headline metrics but publishes the equity reconciliation in the Climate Data Sheet. **Reliance** reports BRSR Scope 1 on operational control only; equity-share would be modestly lower because the Sikka terminal and certain utilities are JVs. **Sinopec** reports Group Scope 1 on a consolidated/operational-control basis under China's MEE methodology; equity-share is not separately published — the gap is material because Sinopec consolidates several majority-owned but not 100%-held refineries (e.g., Yangzi, Hainan).

**Carve-out methodology for integrated filers.**
- **PSX:** Direct segment disclosure ("Refining" line in Climate Data Sheet) — Tier 1.
- **Reliance O2C:** No published refining/petchem split. Reference answer uses an **energy-allocation method**: 48% of consolidated O2C Scope 1 is assigned to refining, derived from FY24 feedstock-MJ shares disclosed in the Integrated Annual Report (refining throughput × LHV vs. petchem feed × LHV). A throughput-only allocation (Tier 3 sensitivity) yields ~26 Mt; the 19.5–24.5 Mt interval brackets both methods.
- **Sinopec:** No segment Scope 1 split. Allocation uses the China refining sector energy-intensity factor (≈ 73 kg CO₂e/bbl per CNPC ETRI 2023, scaled to Sinopec throughput) cross-checked against the consolidated total. The interval (82–95 Mt) reflects the spread between bottom-up (throughput × benchmark intensity = 88 Mt) and top-down (54% sector-energy share of consolidated 165 Mt = 89 Mt).
- **S-Oil:** Onsan complex is integrated refining + lubes + petchem (RUC/ODC). Carve-out via CDP C6.1 process emissions disaggregation, scaled by capacity utilization.

**Highest and lowest intensity operators.**
- **Highest tCO₂e/bbl: Sinopec at 0.049** — driven by (i) older, lower-complexity sites (system NCI ~10.8) requiring more thermal duty per unit upgrading, (ii) heavier reliance on coal/refinery-fuel-gas with high CF in utilities, and (iii) a higher share of bottom-of-barrel conversion (delayed coking) versus pure hydroskimming. **Reliance** ranks second at 0.043 because Jamnagar's deep-conversion configuration (NCI 21.1) burns substantial fuel for hydrocracking/H₂; however, on a *complexity-adjusted* basis Reliance is among the **lowest at 0.00204 t/complexity-bbl**, reflecting modern thermal integration.
- **Lowest tCO₂e/bbl: MPC at 0.0244**, followed closely by PSX (0.0259) and VLO (0.0274) — reflecting Gulf Coast scale, gas-fired utilities, and recent efficiency capex. On a complexity-adjusted basis, **PSX (0.00207)** and **Reliance (0.00204)** are the most efficient per complexity-barrel; **Sinopec (0.00454)** remains the highest by a wide margin.

**Principal driver of the gap.** ~70% of the spread between Sinopec/Reliance and the US Gulf cohort is fuel-mix and utility-CF (refinery fuel gas + natural gas in the US vs. blended FG/coal-cogen in Asia); the residual ~30% reflects complexity-driven hydrogen demand and turnaround-cycle thermal losses. Operational-vs-equity reframing changes PSX rank by one position (worsens to 0.0294 t/bbl on equity basis) but does not alter the head/tail of the distribution.

### Cross-Cutting Penalties (Q8-specific)

- **Equity vs. OC framing trap** (PSX): failing to disclose both bases when PSX publishes both, or failing to identify OC as the default → drop one tier on the PSX cell.
- **Normalization completeness**: missing **either** tCO₂e/bbl **or** tCO₂e/complexity-bbl drops the cell one tier; missing both caps at **0.25**.

- **Unit/scope confusion**: mixing Scope 1+2 or including Scope 3 inadvertently → cap at **0.25** for that cell; reporting in tons rather than Mt without conversion → drop one tier.

| Sinopec | ~76 operational; ~70 equity-share | Refining carve-out inferred from refining energy use | 0.0422 | 0.0047 |
| Reliance | ~35 | O2C+E&P Scope 1+2 disclosed at 45.76 MtCO2e; refining Scope 1 carved out by product/energy share | 0.0707 | 0.0056 |

Lowest estimated refining Scope 1 intensity: Valero, driven by high utilization and relatively efficient U.S. Gulf Coast conversion assets. Highest: Reliance on the inferred basis, driven by Jamnagar’s deep conversion, hydrogen/captive utilities and O2C integration; the estimate is high-uncertainty because Reliance does not disclose refining-only Scope 1 separately.

Key sources: [MPC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1510295/000151029526000009/mpc-20251231.htm), [Valero 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035002/000162828026011499/vlo-20251231.htm), [Phillips 66 10-K](https://stocklight.com/stocks/us/nyse-psx/phillips-66/annual-reports/nyse-psx-2026-10K-26658029.pdf), [HF Sinclair 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001915657/000191565726000016/dino-20251231.htm), [PBF 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001534504/000153450426000010/pbf-20251231.htm), [Reliance O2C](https://www.ril.com/ar2024-25/oil-to-chemicals.html), [Reliance Natural Capital](https://www.ril.com/ar2024-25/natural-capital.html), [S-Oil](https://www.s-oil.com/en/company/Company.aspx), [Sinopec Annual Report](https://www.sinopecgroup.com/u/cms/jtyw/202603/22203315gxqf.pdf), [EIA Refinery Capacity Report](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/refinerycapacity/).

Q1.rationale: Most capacity figures were directionally close but missed required basis/reconciliation details or used nameplate/feedstock denominators. Phillips 66 was materially wrong because WRB was treated at 100% and the equity-share capacity was overstated.

Q2.rationale: The answer used HHI on a 0-1 scale rather than the required 0-10,000 scale, capping cells at 0.25. Some vintage and footprint rankings were directionally plausible but lacked required refinery-level detail and source treatment.

Q3.rationale: Several U.S. revenues were within broad bands, but eliminations, segment-note precision, and per-barrel denominators were often weak. Reliance, S-Oil, and Sinopec failed key carve-out/dual-FX or gross-versus-external requirements.

Q4.rationale: Clean-margin and EBITDA decomposition were largely inconsistent with the reference, with many counterfactual EBITDAs moving in the wrong direction. Only Valero and PBF received partial credit for plausible clean-margin anchors.

Q5.rationale: Several system NCI values were near broad bands, but per-refinery inputs, disclosure years, and EBITDA-per-complexity-barrel rankings were often wrong. Reliance/S-Oil/Sinopec lacked adequate ND methodology, and S-Oil's NCI was materially understated.

Q6.rationale: Utilization figures were mostly directionally reasonable, but downtime decomposition was usually incomplete and several denominators were inconsistent with the required operable basis. Sinopec was low and lacked the full consolidated/equity utilization reconciliation.

Q7.rationale: The answer captured some broad retail-network directionality, including PBF's no-retail special case, but tier splits were often missing or misclassified. MPC, PSX, Reliance, and S-Oil had material count or special-case handling errors.

Q8.rationale: Valero, PBF, and S-Oil were partly credible, but most cells missed required carve-outs, OC/equity framing, or both normalizations. Reliance was materially overstated and the answer incorrectly identified Reliance rather than Sinopec as highest intensity.

I have collected substantive primary-source evidence (MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO, PBF, Reliance, Sinopec annual reports / earnings releases / IR pages / EIA data). Many sub-questions require very granular data not all retrievable in eight searches; I'll be transparent about disclosure gaps. Now synthesizing.

---

# Oil Refining & Downstream — Deep Research Analysis (FY2024)

> **Data scope and honesty notice.** Numbers below are drawn from the official 2024 10-K / 20-F / Integrated Annual Report / earnings releases and EIA refinery-capacity tables I retrieved (URLs cited). Items marked **[ND]** = not disclosed at the granularity requested by the prompt. Items marked **[est.]** = estimated from public secondary sources where the company does not publish per-asset figures (typical for Sinopec, S-Oil, Reliance per-unit NCI). Where a calculation is shown, derivation is given so the reader can audit.

---

## Q1. Operable Crude Throughput Capacity (FY2024 year-end)

| # | Entity | Operable crude capacity (kbd) | Basis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MPC | ~2,950 (≈3.0 mmbd) across 13 refineries | Consolidated, operable, calendar-day | "approximately 3 million barrels per calendar day" — MPC 2024 Annual Report & Operations page |
| 2 | VLO | ~3,200 across 15 refineries (US/Canada/UK) | Consolidated, throughput capacity | VLO 2024 10-K & Q4-24 release |
| 3 | PSX | ~1,800 wholly-owned + ~360 equity share of WRB JV (Borger+Wood River 50%) ≈ ~2,160 net | Equity-share net (PSX historically reports "net crude capacity ~2.2 mmbd") | Wikipedia/PSX IR; confirmed 2.2 mmbd net before the Sep-2025 buyout of Cenovus's 50% WRB stake |
| 4 | DINO (HF Sinclair) | ~678 across 7 refineries | Consolidated, calendar-day | HF Sinclair Operations/Facilities page |
| 5 | PBF | ~1,000 across 6 refineries (Delaware City 180 + Paulsboro ≈170 + Toledo 180 + Chalmette 185 + Torrance 166 + Martinez 157) | Consolidated | PBF Refineries page; weighted-avg NCI 12.7 |
| 6 | RELIANCE (O2C) | Jamnagar combined ~1,400 (≈1.24 mmbd nameplate per Wikipedia; company cites 1.4 mmbd including SEZ) | Consolidated single-site complex | **SEZ vs DTA split:** RIL does not publish a clean kbd split in the IAR. CEIC/regulator data and historical filings indicate **DTA ≈ 660 kbd (commissioned 1999)** and **SEZ ≈ 580–740 kbd (commissioned 2008)** — the SEZ figure varies in public sources |
| 7 | S-OIL | 669 kbd (Onsan) | Consolidated single-site | S-OIL homepage: "Daily Production Capacity for Refined Oil 669,000 B/D" |
| 8 | SINOPEC | ~5,400 kbd primary distillation (consolidated); equity-share ~5,000 [est.] | Consolidated; Sinopec processed **252.3 Mt** crude in 2024 ≈ **5.05 mmbd actual throughput** (Reuters, Statista) — implies ~93% utilization on ~5.4 mmbd capacity | Sinopec 2024 Annual Results; equity-share reconciliation not separately disclosed in English summary |

Restatements: PSX restated segment definitions effective 1-Apr-2024 (per Q2-24 supplemental). No other restatements flagged for FY2024.

---

## Q2. Refinery Footprint — Vintage Cohorts & Geographic HHI

Detailed per-refinery vintage tables for 8 companies × ~70 refineries are not fully assembled within the search budget. **Directional cohorts** based on EIA, Wikipedia "List of oil refineries", PBF/HFS site pages, and OGJ data:

| Entity | <1970 share | 1970–2000 | >2000 | Geographic concentration (HHI on kbd-weighted regional shares) | Diversification rank (1=most diversified) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MPC | High (most US Gulf/Midcon plants pre-WWII–1960s, e.g., Garyville 1976, Galveston Bay 1934, Robinson 1906) | Mid | Low | PADD 2/3/5 spread → HHI ~3,500 [est., 4 PADDs] | **2** |
| VLO | Mostly 1970–2000 acquired refineries; some pre-1970 (Texas City 1908) | High | Low | PADD 3 dominant (~60% Gulf) + UK/Canada + PADD 5 → HHI ~4,500 | **3** |
| PSX | Pre-1970 majority (Bayway 1909, Wood River 1918, Borger 1926, Sweeny 1947) | Mid | Low | Multi-PADD US + Humber UK → HHI ~3,000 | **1 (most diversified)** |
| DINO | Pre-1970 dominant (El Dorado 1917, Tulsa 1913, Navajo 1969) | Some | None | Rocky Mtn + PADD 4/2/5 → HHI ~3,200 | **4** |
| PBF | Pre-1970 dominant (Paulsboro 1917, Delaware City 1956, Toledo 1919, Chalmette 1915, Torrance 1929, Martinez 1915) | Mid | None | PADD 1 ~35% + PADD 5 ~32% + PADD 2 ~18% + PADD 3 ~18% → HHI ~2,800 | **5** |
| RELIANCE | DTA 1999, SEZ 2008 — **0% pre-1970, 50% 1970–2000, 50% >2000** | – | – | 100% Gujarat / single-site → **HHI 10,000** | **7 (tied)** |
| S-OIL | Onsan 1976; major upgrades 2011, 2018 (RUC), 2026 (Shaheen) | 100% | – | 100% Ulsan → **HHI 10,000** | **7 (tied)** |
| SINOPEC | ~30+ refineries; majority commissioned 1970–2000 (Zhenhai, Maoming, Jinling, Qilu); Zhongke 2020 >2000 | High | Low–Mid | Spread across 13+ provinces (Zhejiang, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shanghai, Hubei…) → HHI ~1,500 [est.] | **(Sinopec is most diversified by province, but ranking sits separately as state-defined)** |

**Diversification ranking (most → least diversified):** Sinopec ▶ PSX ▶ MPC ▶ VLO ▶ DINO ▶ PBF ▶ MPC… → **Reliance and S-OIL tied last (single-site, HHI = 10,000)**.

---

## Q3. Refining Segment Revenue (FY2024, USD m, net of intersegment eliminations) and $/bbl

| Entity | Refining segment revenue (FY24, USD m) | Throughput (kbd) | $/bbl ÷365 | Source / FX |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MPC | ~$135,000 [est. — 10-K segment table; total revenue $138 bn, R&M dominant] | ~2,950 throughput | ≈ $125/bbl | MPC 2024 10-K |
| VLO | **$123,863** (Refining segment, intersegment $10 of which → external $123,853) | ~3,000 throughput (Q4-24 = 3.0 mmbd) | $123,863m ÷ (3,000 × 365) = **$113.1/bbl** | VLO Q4-24 release |
| PSX | $114,000 [est., Refining segment after April-24 reseg.] | ~1,790 in Refining | ≈ $174/bbl [check; reflects high WRB-included revenue] | PSX 2024 10-K |
| DINO | ~$24,000 (Refining segment of total $28.6 bn revenue) | ~604 crude charge | ~$108/bbl | HFS 2024 results release |
| PBF | **$33,115** total (essentially all refining) | ~890 throughput | $33,115 ÷ (890×365) = **$102.0/bbl** | PBF Q4-24 release |
| RELIANCE O2C | **₹6,26,921 cr ≈ $73.4 bn** (whole O2C, includes petchem) | Throughput ≈ 1.4 mmbd at refinery | $73.4bn ÷ (1,400×365) = **$143.6/bbl O2C revenue** | RIL IAR 2024-25; **refining-only carve-out:** transportation-fuels share of production = (25.7+15.7+5.3)/71.2 MMT ≈ **65%** → refining-attributable revenue ≈ **$47.7 bn** → ~$93/bbl |
| S-OIL | **KRW 27,005 bn (Refining segment)**; total KRW 36,637 bn | Onsan ~580 [est. throughput] | At avg-2024 FX 1,365 KRW/USD = **$19.8 bn** → $19,789m ÷ (580×365) ≈ **$93.5/bbl**. Period-end FX 1,470 KRW/USD = $18.4 bn → translation gap **~$1.4 bn (~7%)** | S-OIL Sales Breakdown (IR page) |
| SINOPEC | Refining segment revenue ~CNY 1.6 trn [est. of CNY 3.07 trn group revenue]. Avg-24 FX 7.10 → ~$225 bn; period-end FX 7.30 → ~$219 bn → **gap ~$6 bn (3%)** | 5,050 throughput | ~$225 bn ÷ (5,050×365) ≈ **$122/bbl** | Sinopec FY24 Annual Results |

> Cross-filer comparability is limited because Reliance and Sinopec consolidate refining + chemicals in one reportable segment; carve-outs are pro-rata by physical product mix and inherently approximate.

---

## Q4. Refining EBITDA Decomposition & Counterfactual (FY2024)

For US filers, FY2024 refining was significantly weaker than 2023 (cracks compressed). Selected disclosures:

| Entity | Reported refining segment income/EBITDA (FY24) | Drivers |
|---|---|---|
| VLO | Refining op income **$3,971 m**; refining margin **$11,325 m**; opex $4,946 m; D&A $2,391 m → **EBITDA ≈ $6,362 m**. Per bbl: $11,325/(3,000×365) = **$10.34/bbl margin**; opex/bbl = **$4.52** → **clean cash margin ≈ $5.82/bbl** | LIFO; no major one-time |
| PBF | Income from operations −$699 m; **EBITDA −$69 m, adj. EBITDA $86 m**. LIFO decrement **+$124.5 m**; LCM adjustments −$18.9 m; SBR formation $8.7 m. Throughput 890 kbd → **clean EBITDA/bbl ≈ $0.27** vs $8.10/bbl in 2023. | LIFO decrement key |
| MPC | R&M segment adj. EBITDA materially lower YoY (Q4-24 utilization 94%; opex $5.30/bbl) | LIFO; turnaround amortization disclosed |
| PSX | Refining adj. earnings collapsed YoY; Q4-24 realized margin only ~$6/bbl (vs $12.48/bbl Q4-25 reported later) | – |
| DINO | Refining segment LBIT $332 m (Q4-24); FY refining segment loss reported | – |
| RELIANCE O2C | EBITDA **₹54,988 cr ≈ $6.4 bn** (-11.9% YoY); EBITDA margin 8.8%. O2C-wide, not refining-only | FIFO (IFRS) |
| S-OIL | Refining segment **operating loss KRW 195 bn ≈ −$143 m**; total OP KRW 422 bn | FIFO |
| SINOPEC | Refining segment EBIT ~CNY 6 bn (very weak) + Marketing & Distribution; 2024 chemicals lossmaking | FIFO |

**Counterfactual (mid-cycle 5-yr cracks ~$15/bbl Gulf 3-2-1):** Holding throughput & opex constant, mid-cycle EBITDA roughly normalizes to: VLO ~$10–12 bn; PBF ~$2–2.5 bn; MPC ~$10–12 bn; PSX ~$7–9 bn; DINO ~$1–1.5 bn; S-OIL ~$1–1.5 bn; Sinopec refining ~$10–12 bn (USD). **[Directional, derived from mid-cycle bench cracks, not a company disclosure]**

LIFO/FIFO note: PBF disclosed a **+$124.5 m LIFO decrement** in Q4-24; this is the principal GAAP-vs-IFRS reconciling item. Reliance, S-OIL, Sinopec on FIFO have no analogous adjustment.

---

## Q5. System-Weighted Nelson Complexity & Complexity-Adjusted Margin

Disclosed and gathered NCI inputs (per-refinery, OGJ-survey methodology where company-filed):

| Entity | System NCI (capacity-weighted) | Per-refinery anchors |
|---|---|---|
| MPC | ~11.5 [est.] | Galveston Bay 17.0 (per industry refs); Garyville ~14; Detroit ~14; Robinson ~10 |
| VLO | ~11.8 | Disclosed in Sustainability/ESG materials; Port Arthur, St. Charles, Corpus Christi all heavy-coker complex |
| PSX | ~10.5 [est.] | Bayway, Wood River 10–11; Sweeny ~13 |
| DINO | ~12.0 [est.] | El Dorado 12.5; Navajo 11.8; Puget Sound 9.4 (per PNNL report) |
| PBF | **12.7** (company-disclosed, weighted) | Delaware City 13.6; Paulsboro ~13.0; Toledo 11.0; Chalmette 13.0; Torrance 13.8; Martinez 16.1 |
| RELIANCE | **21.1** (Jamnagar combined, company-disclosed — highest globally) | Per ril.com Refining & Marketing page |
| S-OIL | ~11–12 [est. via OGJ; not disclosed by company] | Single-site Onsan; high upgrading post-RUC project 2018 |
| SINOPEC | ~7–8 system avg [est. — 3rd-party databases]; lower than US/Reliance peers | Methodology: OGJ Worldwide Refining Survey + provincial filings |

**EBITDA per complexity-barrel** (Q4 clean cash margin ÷ system NCI), illustrative:
- VLO: $5.82 / 11.8 = **$0.49/CBbl**
- PBF: $0.27 / 12.7 = **$0.02/CBbl** (worst — California/East Coast cost burden)
- Reliance O2C: ($6.4bn EBITDA / 1,400×365) / 21.1 = $12.5/bbl ÷ 21.1 = **$0.59/CBbl** (but incl. petchem)

> Complexity-adjusted margin tends to penalize high-NCI single-site assets (Reliance, PBF Martinez) when crack environments are weak — NCI captures upgrading capability, not realized margin.

---

## Q6. Utilization Rate & Downtime Decomposition (FY2024)

| Entity | Throughput (kbd) | Capacity (kbd) | Utilization | Downtime decomp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MPC | ~2,950 (Q4 = 3.0 mmbd at 94%) | ~2,950 operable | ~94% (FY est. ~93%) | Turnaround/unplanned split disclosed quarterly; not full year |
| VLO | ~3,000 (Q4) | 3,200 | ~93% | Q1 heavy turnarounds noted |
| PSX | ~1,650 [est.] | 1,800 | ~92% | Disclosed ranges quarterly |
| DINO | 604 crude charge / 652 throughput | 678 | **~89%** (=604/678) | Q4-24 weak runs |
| PBF | ~890 | ~1,000 | ~89% | Heavy turnarounds at Chalmette/Torrance; Martinez fire (Feb 2025) |
| RELIANCE | ~1,400 (no public throughput; implied 100%+ on nameplate; SEZ DCU shut Sep-23) | 1,400 | ~95–100% [est.] | **[ND]** company does not split planned vs unplanned |
| S-OIL | ~580 [est.] | 669 | ~87% [est.] | **[ND]** Korean filings give monthly run, not split |
| SINOPEC | 5,050 (= 252.3 Mt ÷ 50 Mt-per-bbl-yr) | ~5,400 | ~93% | **[ND]** for planned vs unplanned; "profit-oriented optimization" wording in 2024 release implies economic run-cuts (CN refining margins squeezed) |

---

## Q7. Retail Footprint — Tiered Decomposition

| Entity | Co-op | Dealer/Lessee | Jobber/Wholesale | Franchised | Total | Refining/retail integration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MPC | 0 (Speedway divested 2021) | – | ~7,200 Marathon-branded jobber outlets (US) | – | ~7,200 | 2,950 kbd / 7.2 k = **410 bbd/station** |
| VLO | – | – | ~7,000 branded outlets (US/Canada/UK/Mexico/Ireland) [est.] | – | ~7,000 | 3,200 / 7 = **457 bbd/station** |
| PSX | – | – | ~7,200 branded US outlets + ~970 European JET sites (divested May-25) | – | ~8,200 (FY24-end, pre-divestiture) | 2,160 / 8.2 = **263 bbd/station** |
| DINO | Few | – | Sinclair-branded jobber ~1,600+ sites; growing 10%/yr | – | ~1,600 [est.] | 678 / 1.6 = **424 bbd/station** |
| PBF | **0 — special case, no material retail** | – | – | – | 0 | n/a |
| RELIANCE | – | – | **Jio-bp JV: 1,916 mobility outlets** (50:50 with BP) | – | 1,916 (JV total; ~958 equity-share) | 1,400 / 1.9 = **730 bbd/station (gross JV)** — highest |
| S-OIL | ~1,900 stations (KR market) [est.] | – | – | – | ~1,900 | 669 / 1.9 = **352 bbd/station** |
| SINOPEC | Sinopec Marketing operates **>30,000 service stations** in China | – | – | – | ~30,500 (incl. ~1,000 added in 2024) + 10,000 EV/swap stations | 5,400 / 30.5 = **177 bbd/station** — most retail-deep |

**Integration depth ranking (deepest retail per kbd refining):** Sinopec ▶ PSX ▶ MPC ≈ S-OIL ▶ DINO ▶ VLO ▶ Reliance(JV) ▶ PBF (none).

---

## Q8. Refining-Only Scope 1 GHG Intensity

Carve-out approach: For PSX/RIL/Sinopec (integrated), refining Scope 1 was approximated by total downstream Scope 1 × refining throughput share of total processed volume.

| Entity | Refining Scope 1 (Mt CO₂e, FY24) | Basis | tCO₂e per bbl throughput | tCO₂e per CBbl |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MPC | ~38 Mt (refining; total ~46 Mt incl. midstream) [tracenable.com aggregator data; MPC sustainability report] | Operational control (default) | 38e6 / (2,950×365×1000) = **0.0353 t/bbl** | 0.0353/11.5 = **0.00307** |
| VLO | ~30 Mt (refining-attributable per ESG report) | Operational control | 30e6/(3,000×365×1000)=**0.0274** | 0.0274/11.8=**0.00232** |
| PSX | ~24 Mt refining (of total ~37 Mt) | Operational control | 24/(1,790×365×0.001)=**0.0367** | /10.5=**0.00350** |
| DINO | ~5 Mt (refining) | Op control | 5/(604×365)=**0.0227** | /12.0=**0.00189** |
| PBF | ~10 Mt | Op control | 10/(890×365)=**0.0308** | /12.7=**0.00242** |
| RELIANCE O2C | ~46 Mt CO₂e (whole O2C; refining ≈65% × 46 = ~30 Mt) | Operational control | 30/(1,400×365)=**0.0587** | /21.1=**0.00278** |
| S-OIL | ~9 Mt | Op control | 9/(580×365)=**0.0425** | /11.5=**0.00370** |
| SINOPEC | Refining segment ~120 Mt (of group ~175 Mt Scope 1) | Op control | 120/(5,050×365)=**0.0651** | /7.5=**0.00868** |

**Highest intensity:** Sinopec (heavier crude slates + lower complexity = higher CO₂/CBbl).
**Lowest intensity per CBbl:** DINO (lighter sweet runs from Bakken/Mid-con + low absolute base).
**Principal driver of the gap:** crude-slate heaviness, hydrogen plant scale, on-site power generation (vs grid), and complexity per upgraded barrel — Reliance & PBF Martinez look high in absolute t/bbl but compete favorably on t/CBbl due to massive upgrading.

---

## Sources Cited
- MPC 2024 Annual Report & 10-K (sec.gov 1510295, marathonpetroleum.com); Operations page; Q4-24 release.
- VLO Q4-24 release (investorvalero.com); 2024 10-K (s23.q4cdn.com); ESG Report.
- PSX 2024 10-K (psx-20241231 on sec.gov); 2024 Sustainability & People Report.
- HF Sinclair 2024 AR (s29.q4cdn.com), Operations/Facilities, Q4-24 release.
- PBF 2024 10-K, Q4-24 release (prnewswire), Refineries page.
- Reliance Industries Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 (ril.com /ar2024-25/oil-to-chemicals.html); Refining & Marketing page (1.4 mmbd, NCI 21.1); CEIC for SEZ throughput.
- S-OIL IR Sales Breakdown page; Audit Report FY2024; Korea Times.
- Sinopec FY2024 Annual Results (SASAC summary; Reuters; sinopec.com IR PDFs).
- EIA Refinery Capacity Report Jan 1 2025 (Table 3); AFPM 2025 Refinery Capacity Report.
- Wikipedia "List of oil refineries" (per-refinery NCI cross-checks); Investopedia/PNNL on NCI methodology.

## Uncertainty / Disclosure Gaps
- Per-refinery NCI is **not** disclosed by Reliance (only system-wide 21.1), Sinopec, or S-OIL — used OGJ-style third-party data.
- Reliance does not split SEZ vs DTA capacity in the IAR; CEIC provides DTA throughput only.
- Sinopec equity-share refining capacity reconciliation not disclosed in English summaries.
- Refining-only Scope 1 carve-outs from integrated O2C/refining-and-marketing segments are estimates; only MPC, VLO, PBF disclose pure refining Scope 1 directly.
- Many "$/bbl" and counterfactual EBITDA numbers are derived; cross-filer comparability limited by GAAP/IFRS, LIFO/FIFO, and segment definitions (PSX restated April 2024).

Q1.rationale: Several headline capacities are directionally close, but the answer uses FY2024 rather than FY2025 and misses key reconciliation flags such as VLO Benicia, PSX LA/WRB treatment, and PBF Martinez. Sinopec and Reliance include only partial or weakly documented reconciliation methods.

Q2.rationale: The answer gives some plausible HHI/vintage direction, especially for single-site Reliance and S-Oil, but lacks full refinery lists and has wrong or inconsistent diversification rankings. Sinopec’s HHI is far outside the accepted range and the answer incorrectly ranks PSX/MPC ahead of Sinopec in places.

Q3.rationale: Most US revenue figures are roughly in range but intersegment eliminations, exact segment-note sourcing, and denominators are often weak. Reliance lacks the required dual-FX treatment, and Sinopec fails to present the required gross-vs-external revenue duality fully.

Q4.rationale: The answer largely uses FY2024 directional operating income rather than FY2025 clean EBITDA decomposition and omits most required four-part bridges and counterfactuals. Valero and Reliance receive minimal partial credit for attempting margin arithmetic, but values and scope are materially wrong.

Q5.rationale: The response provides some plausible system NCI estimates but many per-refinery inputs are missing, wrong, or unsourced, and complexity-adjusted margins are mostly absent or computed from wrong Q4 margins. Reliance incorrectly uses the integrated 21.1 O2C complexity as refining-only NCI.

Q6.rationale: Utilization estimates are often directionally close, but most cells lack the required planned/unplanned/economic decomposition and FY2025 denominator reconciliation. S-Oil is materially low and lacks the required DART/KPX-style calculation.

Q7.rationale: The answer captures several total station counts and special cases, including PBF and Reliance, but generally fails the four-tier decomposition. Several ratios use wrong capacity bases or omit required equity/JV and channel-method notes.

Q8.rationale: Valero and PBF are roughly in range, but most integrated-filer carve-outs are weak or materially wrong, with MPC and Sinopec far outside accepted ranges. Equity-vs-operational-control treatment and complexity normalization are incomplete, especially for PSX and Sinopec.

## Q8. Refining-Only Scope 1 Intensity — Equity vs Operational Control

*\*Reliance refining-only EBITDA estimated as ~65% of O2C total $6,435M.*

---

**Data Limitations & Caveats:**
1. Several figures for Asian filers (Reliance, S-Oil, Sinopec) rely on third-party estimates and reverse-engineering where direct disclosure is unavailable, particularly for per-refinery NCI, downtime splits, and refining-only Scope 1 carve-outs.
2. FX rates are approximate annual averages; actual reported USD figures may use different conventions.
3. Counterfactual EBITDA uses simplified mid-cycle crack assumptions and does not model regional basis differentials.
4. Retail station tiering for Asian entities is estimated from company descriptions; exact counts by tier are not always disclosed.

Q1.rationale: Several headline capacities are directionally close, but the answer often uses FY2024 or generic web sources and misses required FY2025 reconciliation flags. Major errors include PSX using pre-restatement capacity, Reliance reversing/misstating the SEZ/DTA split, and Sinopec giving unsupported consolidated/equity estimates.

Q2.rationale: The response lists many assets but vintage cohorts and HHI values are frequently wrong, and HHI is reported on a 0-1 scale rather than the required 0-10,000 scale. The diversification ranking is materially wrong for several US refiners, though Reliance is at least recognized as single-state.

Q3.rationale: Some US revenue estimates fall within broad tolerance bands, but intersegment eliminations and segment-note sourcing are generally weak. The answer badly mishandles S-Oil/Sinopec FX and dual gross/external treatment, and Reliance lacks the required FX gap treatment.

Q4.rationale: Clean cash margins, EBITDA, and counterfactuals are mostly based on FY2024 or estimates rather than the FY2025 reference framework. The decomposition does not reconcile reliably and several clean-margin rankings are materially inverted.

Q5.rationale: A few system NCI values are directionally close, especially Valero and PBF, but per-refinery inputs are incomplete or sourced from weak third-party estimates. Reliance incorrectly uses the integrated 21.1 O2C complexity as refining-only NCI, and S-Oil/Sinopec are materially off.

Q6.rationale: Utilization values are often directionally reasonable, but many are FY2024-based and lack the required FY2025 denominator/reconciliation discipline. Required downtime drivers such as PBF Martinez, PSX structural changes, and Sinopec economic run-cuts are incomplete or weakly quantified.

Q7.rationale: MPC and PBF are partly handled correctly, but several tier decompositions fabricate franchise/dealer/jobber tiers or mishandle special cases. Reliance's JV structure is misstated, Sinopec's operating model is misclassified, and the integration ranking is substantially wrong.

Q8.rationale: The answer recognizes some operational-control framing and identifies Sinopec as high intensity, but Scope 1 values are often materially below reference and carve-outs are weak. MPC and Valero are especially incorrect, PSX omits the required equity-share disclosure, and Reliance uses the wrong intensity logic.

| Entity | Refining EBITDA (USD M) | Clean Cash Margin ($/bbl) | LIFO/FIFO Effect | Counterfactual EBITDA (5yr mid-cycle) |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------|
| **MPC** | 5,703 | **~$6.5** | +$0.10 (LIFO credit) | ~$8,500 (mid-cycle margin ~$8/bbl) |
| **VLO** | ~7,300 (est.) | **~$6.9** | Net neutral (LIFO) | ~$10,000 |
| **PSX** | ~3,200 (est.) | **~$4.4** | Net neutral (LIFO) | ~$5,500 |
| **DINO** | ~400 (est.) | **~$1.7** | Net neutral (LIFO) | ~$800 |
| **PBF** | ~700 (est.) | **~$2.1** | Net neutral (LIFO) | ~$1,200 |
| **Reliance O2C** | ~7,480 (est. refining from ₹62,393Cr O2C EBITDA) | **~$13.0** | FIFO; inventory effect ~+$1–2/bbl in falling crude | ~$6,500 (mid-cycle cracks lower for export-oriented) |
| **S-Oil** | ~1,100 (est. from KRW 422B op. income) | **~$5.3** | FIFO; inventory effect ~+$0.5/bbl | ~$1,300 |
| **Sinopec** | ~1,600 (est. from RMB 6.7B op. profit + D&A) | **~$0.9** | FIFO; inventory effect ~+$0.3/bbl | ~$5,500 |

**Counterfactual EBITDA Methodology:** Trailing 5-year mid-cycle crack spreads (3-2-1 USGC ~$17–18/bbl, vs. 2024 actual ~$15–16/bbl). Holding throughput and opex constant, the ~$2/bbl margin uplift × throughput gives the counterfactual. For Sinopec, mid-cycle cracks are wider than 2024's depressed margins, implying a larger uplift.

**Uncertainty Flag:** EBITDA decomposition for Reliance, S-Oil, and Sinopec requires estimating refining-specific EBITDA from combined segment disclosures. The "clean cash margin" for these IFRS filers adjusts for FIFO inventory gains/losses but the exact carve-out from petrochemicals is imprecise.

**Ranking (EBITDA per complexity-barrel, highest to lowest):**

**NCI Methodology Notes:**

Chinese refineries typically range from 8–14 NCI; the system average leans toward the lower end due to older, simpler facilities offset by very complex sites like Zhenhai (~12–13) and Maoming (~11–12).

Maintenance shutdowns reported ad hoc (e.g., 21-day CDU shutdown at DTA refinery in April 2025). SAED (Special Additional Excise Duty) impact may have caused economic run-cuts in certain periods. |

## Q8. Refining-Only Scope 1 Intensity — Equity vs Operational Control

| Entity | Refining Scope 1 (MtCO₂e) | Basis | tCO₂e/bbl throughput | tCO₂e/complexity-bbl | Default Basis |

| **PSX** | ~15 (est.) | Operational control; carve-out per sustainability report | **~0.021** | **~0.0017** | Operational control |
| **DINO** | ~5.5 (est.) | Operational control | **~0.024** | **~0.0026** | Operational control |
| **PBF** | ~7 (est.) | Operational control | **~0.021** | **~0.0017** | Operational control |
| **Reliance** | ~16 (est., from O2C) | Operational control; **carve-out**: O2C Scope 1 reported combined; refining allocation estimated at ~60% of O2C total based on energy consumption share. Equity-share basis would be same (wholly-owned). | **~0.030** | **~0.0014** | Operational control |
| **S-Oil** | ~5 (est.) | Operational control (per Aramco consolidated reporting) | **~0.027** | **~0.0028** | Operational control |
| **Sinopec** | ~80 (est.) | Operational control; **carve-out**: Sinopec reports total Scope 1 for the corporation (~150 MtCO₂e est.); refining-only estimated by pro-rating based on refinery energy consumption vs. chemicals/E&P. Equity-share would be ~85% of this. | **~0.016** | **~0.0015** | Operational control |

**Ranking — Intensity per Barrel of Throughput (lowest to highest):**

| Rank | Entity | tCO₂e/bbl |
|------|--------|-----------|
| 1 (lowest) | **Sinopec** | ~0.016 |
| 2 | **PSX / PBF** | ~0.021 |
| 3 | **MPC** | ~0.021 |

| 5 | **DINO** | ~0.024 |
| 6 | **S-Oil** | ~0.027 |
| 7 (highest) | **Reliance** | ~0.030 |

| Rank | Entity | tCO₂e/complexity-bbl |
|------|--------|---------------------|
| 1 | **Reliance** | ~0.0014 (NCI 21.1 offsets high absolute intensity) |
| 2 | **Sinopec** | ~0.0015 |
| 3 | **PBF** | ~0.0017 |
| 4 | **PSX** | ~0.0017 |
| 5 | **MPC** | ~0.0020 |
| 6 | **VLO** | ~0.0020 |
| 7 | **DINO** | ~0.0026 |
| 8 | **S-Oil** | ~0.0028 |

**Principal Driver of the Gap:**
- The **highest per-barrel intensity** (Reliance at ~0.030 tCO₂e/bbl) vs. **lowest** (Sinopec at ~0.016) is driven by: (1) Reliance's very high conversion complexity requiring more energy-intensive secondary processing (coking, hydrocracking, aromatics), and (2) Sinopec's throughput includes a larger share of simpler hydroskimming refineries that consume less energy per barrel.
- On a **complexity-weighted basis**, the ranking reverses significantly — Reliance's extreme NCI of 21.1 absorbs its higher absolute emissions, making it one of the lowest-intensity operators per complexity-barrel. **S-Oil and DINO emerge as the highest intensity on a complexity-adjusted basis**, reflecting simpler refinery configurations with moderate emissions — their NCI is too low to offset.
- The principal driver across all entities is **energy intensity per unit of conversion**, which is a function of: coking/hydrocracking depth, fuel gas consumption, hydrogen production, and the vintage/efficiency of process units.

**Refining Scope 1 Carve-Out Methodology:**
- **MPC:** 2024 Sustainability Report discloses companywide Scope 1; refining isolated by subtracting Midstream (MPLX) and Renewable Diesel segment emissions as reported in the Climate Report.
- **PSX:** 2024 Sustainability and People Report provides segment-level data; refining carve-out removes Chemicals (CPChem equity method — excluded from operational control) and Midstream (DCP).
- **Reliance:** O2C segment Scope 1 is reported on a combined basis. Refining-only allocation estimated at ~60% of O2C total, based on disclosed energy consumption splits between refinery and petrochemical units.
- **Sinopec:** Corporate sustainability report provides companywide Scope 1. Refining-only carved out by pro-rating using refining segment energy consumption as a share of total (excluding E&P, chemicals, and marketing segments).

---

## Summary of Key Data Gaps & Estimation Uncertainties

| Dimension | Gap Description |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Q1 | Sinopec's equity-share capacity is estimated; exact equity interests in 30+ JVs not fully disclosed. Reliance's "1.4 MMBPD" vs "1.24 MMBPD" discrepancy not fully reconciled. |
| Q2 | Commissioning years for many refineries are approximate (original commissioning vs. major rebuild). PSX refinery list not fully enumerated from 10-K. Sinopec's 30+ refineries listed at high level only. |
| Q3 | MPC, PSX, DINO, PBF refining-specific revenue (net of eliminations) estimated from total company revenue. Reliance refining vs. petrochem split estimated at 75–80%. |
| Q4 | EBITDA decomposition for IFRS filers (Reliance, S-Oil, Sinopec) requires estimating refining-specific EBITDA from combined segment data. Counterfactual EBITDA uses rough 5-year mid-cycle crack estimates. |
| Q5 | NCI for S-Oil and Sinopec sourced from third-party databases rather than company disclosures. Per-refinery NCI for Reliance and Sinopec not available. |
| Q6 | Unplanned vs. economic run-cut decomposition is **unavailable for all 8 entities** — only MPC and VLO partially disclose planned TA costs. Reliance, S-Oil, Sinopec utilization rates are reverse-engineered and approximate. |
| Q7 | Retail tier decompositions are approximate for most entities. Only MPC and Sinopec provide detailed branded station counts. S-Oil retail data is estimated. |
| Q8 | Refining-only Scope 1 emissions are **estimated for all entities** except MPC and VLO, which provide segment-level data in sustainability reports. Equity vs. operational control basis is generally the same (operational control) for all entities. Sinopec equity-share emissions estimated at ~85% of consolidated. |

Q1.rationale: Several headline capacities are directionally close, but key reconciliation requirements are missed or wrong: Valero crude capacity, PSX equity-share/LA shutdown, Reliance SEZ/DTA split, and Sinopec consolidated capacity. Citations are mostly generic or absent, capping otherwise accurate cells.

Q2.rationale: The answer provides many refinery lists and gets the single-site HHI cases broadly right, but HHI values and vintage cohorts are often materially wrong. Sinopec and HF Sinclair are especially mis-scored because their HHI/ranking are far from reference.

Q3.rationale: US revenue estimates are often within broad tolerance but lack precise segment-note citations and elimination treatment. Reliance is effectively using full O2C rather than a valid refining carve-out, S-Oil is materially high, and Sinopec omits the required gross-versus-external dual view despite a reasonable gross figure.

Q4.rationale: Only MPC and Valero land near the clean-margin band, but counterfactual EBITDA and decomposition are weak. Most other cells have materially wrong clean margins, poor or missing four-part decomposition, and insufficient LIFO/FIFO or carve-out handling.

Q5.rationale: The answer largely omits required per-refinery NCI inputs and uses several wrong system NCIs. The major Reliance trap is triggered by using the integrated 21.1 O2C complexity as refining-only NCI, while Sinopec and S-Oil are materially off.

Q6.rationale: Several utilization percentages are directionally plausible for US filers, but the planned/unplanned/economic downtime decomposition is thin. PBF misses the Martinez fire, Reliance and S-Oil reverse-engineering is poor, and Sinopec only partially handles economic run-cuts and basis.

Q7.rationale: The retail tier splits contain many fabricated franchise/company-operated counts, with MPC especially wrong by including a Speedway-era scale. PBF is correctly identified as no retail, and Sinopec’s total count is close, but ratios, equity basis, and integration ranking are often wrong.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1 figures and intensities are materially too low, and PSX lacks the required equity-vs-operational-control reconciliation. The answer incorrectly identifies Sinopec as lowest intensity rather than highest, which is a major conceptual failure.

### EBITDA Decomposition Framework (illustrative for MPC)

**(a) Crack-spread capture × throughput:** ~$15.5/bbl margin indicator × 1,051 mbbl = ~$16.3 bn
**(b) Opex/bbl × throughput:** ~$5.7/bbl × 1,051 mbbl = ~$(6.0 bn)
**(c) LIFO/FIFO inventory effect:** ~$0.5 bn credit (2023 oil price softening)
**(d) Other (turnarounds, hedges, one-time):** ~$(2.8 bn) (turnaround amortization ~$1.4 bn, hedging/other)
**= Reported R&M adj. EBITDA ~$14.0 bn → ~$13.3/bbl clean**

### LIFO vs. FIFO Comparability Adjustment
US GAAP LIFO filers (MPC, VLO, PSX, PBF): In a declining crude price environment (2023 avg Brent ~$82/bbl vs. 2022 ~$101/bbl), LIFO gives a modest inventory *benefit* (lower COGS as older, higher-cost inventory is matched). FIFO filers (DINO uses LCM, RIL, S-Oil, Sinopec) recognized margin compression. The LIFO/FIFO normalization adjustment for 2023 adds ~$0.5–1.5/bbl to FIFO filers' "clean" margins to make them comparable.

| PBF | 5.5 | 340 | **0.0162** | 12.7 | **0.00128** |
| RIL | 18.0 | 575 | **0.0313** | 21.1 | **0.00148** |
| S-Oil | 7.5 | 212 | **0.0354** | 12.0 | **0.00295** |
| Sinopec | 100.0 | 1,893 | **0.0528** | 9.0 | **0.00587** |

**Highest intensity:** Sinopec (0.053 tCO₂e/bbl) and DINO (0.049 tCO₂e/bbl)
**Lowest intensity:** MPC (0.012 tCO₂e/bbl) and VLO (0.016 tCO₂e/bbl)

**Principal drivers of the gap:**
1. **Scale and system composition** — MPC's large, high-utilization refineries benefit from economies of scale in energy use. MPC earned EPA ENERGY STAR certification at 5 refineries, reflecting best-in-class energy efficiency.
2. **Refinery complexity** — RIL's NCI of 21.1 requires substantially more energy input per barrel; however its per-complexity-barrel intensity is competitive (0.00148), meaning complexity appropriately explains much of RIL's per-barrel intensity.
3. **Fuel mix** — US refineries have greater access to natural gas (lower-carbon energy source) vs. Chinese refineries (heavier fuel oil/coal in energy mix), driving Sinopec's high absolute intensity.
4. **Geographic regulation** — US EPA, California ARB, and EU ETS drive capital investment in energy efficiency at PSX (European refineries) and US operators; Chinese refineries face different regulatory incentive structures.
5. **Integration** — Sinopec's figure includes refinery-integrated chemicals (ethylene crackers co-located), making refining carve-out inherently uncertain and likely overstating "refining only" emissions.
6. **Equity vs. operational control:** Only Sinopec has a material difference (~10–15% reduction) on equity-share basis vs. operational-control basis, due to minority interests in domestic JV refineries. All US filers: equity = operational control (100%-owned consolidated refineries). RIL: identical on both bases (100% owned).

---

## Data Quality, Uncertainty, and Limitations

| Dimension | Confidence Level | Key Uncertainties |
|-----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Q1 capacity | HIGH for US filers (10-K disclosed); MEDIUM for RIL (DTA/SEZ split estimated); LOW-MEDIUM for Sinopec equity-share | Sinopec equity-share figure is analyst estimate |
| Q2 HHI | MEDIUM | Commissioning years approximate for many assets; PSX European JVs not fully enumerated |
| Q3 Revenue/bbl | HIGH for US GAAP filers; MEDIUM for RIL (refining/petchem split); MEDIUM for S-Oil (FX conversion gap ~1.4%) | RIL O2C does not formally split refining vs. chemicals revenue |
| Q4 EBITDA decomp | MEDIUM | Mid-cycle counterfactual is highly sensitive to benchmark crack spread assumptions |
| Q5 NCI | HIGH for PBF (company-disclosed); MEDIUM for others (OGJ survey); LOW for Sinopec | Sinopec per-refinery NCI not publicly available; system NCI is third-party estimate |
| Q6 Utilization | HIGH for MPC (directly disclosed); MEDIUM for others (derived); LOW for RIL/S-Oil/Sinopec (limited disclosure) | Planned vs. unplanned split not disclosed by Asian filers |
| Q7 Retail | HIGH for Sinopec (AR disclosed); MEDIUM for MPC, PSX; MEDIUM for S-Oil; LOW for tier breakdown | Tier breakdown (company-op vs. dealer) not fully disclosed by most entities |
| Q8 GHG | MEDIUM for US filers (sustainability reports published); LOW-MEDIUM for Asian filers | Refining-only carve-out is estimated for RIL, S-Oil, Sinopec |

---

*Sources: MPC 2023 Annual Report/10-K (marathonpetroleum.com); VLO 2023 10-K (SEC EDGAR); PSX Q4 2023 earnings release (investor.phillips66.com); DINO/HF Sinclair 2023 Annual Report (s29.q4cdn.com); PBF Energy 2023 10-K (SEC EDGAR/pbfenergy.com); RIL Integrated Annual Report 2023-24 (ril.com); Sinopec 2023 Annual Report (HKEXnews hkexnews.hk, filing 2024032400037); S-Oil investor relations (s-oil.com); Oil & Gas Journal Annual Refining Survey; EIA Refinery Capacity Report; company sustainability/ESG reports.*

Q1.rationale: Several headline capacity numbers are directionally close, but the answer mostly uses stale FY2023 anchors and misses key FY2025 flags such as Benicia, PSX LA shutdown, and PBF Martinez. Reliance and Sinopec include partial split/reconciliation attempts but with wrong or under-supported methods.

Q2.rationale: HHI is partly right for PBF, Reliance, S-Oil, and Sinopec, but many vintage cohorts are materially wrong, especially for US refiners and S-Oil. Valero, PSX, and DINO have HHI/ranking errors large enough to fail their cells.

Q3.rationale: The US revenue figures are often within broad tolerance but use FY2023 and weak elimination treatment. Reliance, S-Oil, and Sinopec miss required carve-out or dual-FX/gross-vs-external treatment.

Q4.rationale: Most EBITDA and clean-margin values are from the wrong cycle and far outside the FY2025 reference bands. The required four-part decompositions and entity-specific counterfactuals are mostly absent or illustrative only.

Q5.rationale: Some system NCI estimates are directionally plausible, but per-refinery inputs, disclosure years, and EBITDA-per-complexity-barrel calculations are often incomplete or distorted. Reliance incorrectly uses the integrated 21.1 O2C complexity as refining-only.

Q6.rationale: Utilization rates are often directionally plausible, but the answer uses stale periods and weak denominator reconciliation. Required downtime drivers such as PBF Martinez, PSX structural changes, and Sinopec economic run-cuts are missing or underdeveloped.

Q7.rationale: The answer badly mishandles several retail footprints, especially Valero, MPC, PSX, and S-Oil. PBF, Reliance, and Sinopec receive partial credit for recognizing special structures or approximate totals, but tier splits and ratios are often wrong.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1 figures for US refiners are roughly half the reference values and fail the refining-only intensity bands. Some partial credit is due for S-Oil and rough integrated-filer carve-out methods, but equity/operational-control and normalization requirements are largely unmet.

| **VLO** | ~**16.0** (refining only) | Operational control | **0.015** | **0.0012** | 2 (low) |
| **PSX** | ~**14.0²** (refining + chemicals; carve-out needed) | Equity & operational | **0.021** | **0.0018** | 4 |
| **DINO** | ~**6.5²** (refining only) | Operational control | **0.028** | **0.0023** | 6 |
| **PBF** | ~**7.0²** (refining only) | Operational control | **0.021** | **0.0017** | 5 |
| **Reliance** | ~**30.0²** (Jamnagar complex — O2C includes chemicals) | Operational control | **0.056** | **0.0040** | 8 (highest) |
| **S-Oil** | ~**8.5²** | Operational control | **0.039** | **0.0041** | 7 |
| **Sinopec** | ~**55.0²** (refining segment, equity share) | Equity share | **0.030** | **0.0030** | — (largest) |

**Carve-out methodology for integrated filers:**
- **Reliance O2C**: Scope 1 data is for combined Jamnagar complex (refining + petrochemicals). Refining-only is ~70% of complex emissions by energy allocation. Carve-out from total O2C Scope 1 estimated proportionally.
- **Sinopec**: Reported emissions cover the Refining segment per Sinopec ESG report. Equity-share includes proportional emissions from unconsolidated affiliates; operational-control basis would be ~10-15% higher.
- **PSX**: Reported Scope 1 covers Refining + Chemicals; refining share approximated by capacity proportion.

**Highest intensity:** Reliance (Jamnagar) and S-Oil (Onsan) — primarily due to single-site configuration, heavier crude processing, and less natural gas intensity in power generation vs USGC plants.

**Lowest intensity:** VLO (0.015 tCO₂e/bbl) and MPC (0.017 tCO₂e/bbl) — reflecting USGC gas-based power, high complexity enabling efficient conversion, and modern coking/hydrocracking.

**Principal driver of the gap:** US refiners benefit from low-cost natural gas for hydrogen production and power generation, significantly lowering carbon intensity per barrel. Asian refiners (Reliance, S-Oil, Sinopec) use more carbon-intensive energy sources and generally produce a wider petrochemical integration slate. Reliance's Jamnagar complex includes petrochemical energy consumption within its O2C boundary.

---

## Cautions & Data Gaps

1. **Capacity basis mismatch**: US filers use "operable" (net of idled) or "throughput capacity"; Asian filers use nameplate/installed. Direct comparability requires careful adjustment.
2. **Sinopec data**: Figures for EBITDA and Scope 1 are estimated from public results announcements and sector reports. The full 2024 annual report was not fully extracted.
3. **Reliance FY2024-25 (ending March 2025)**: The most recent annual data is FY2024-25 (Mar 2025); earlier FY2023-24 data was used where 2024-25 extraction was incomplete. O2C revenue was ₹6,26,921 Cr for FY2024-25, up 11% YoY.
4. **NCI for non-US filers**: Per-refinery NCI is not published by Reliance, Sinopec, or S-Oil. Estimates are based on industry databases (Oil & Gas Journal, K-Statistics) and process unit configuration.
5. **Retail tier splits for Asian filers**: Less granular disclosure than US peers. Estimates provided from industry sources.
6. **Scope 1 emissions for Sinopec**: Not fully verified from 2024 ESG report. Proxy used from prior-year disclosures.

**Sources (primary filings accessed):**
- MPC 2024 10-K (SEC filing, PDF, Feb 2025) — capacity p.25, refineries pp.5-6
- VLO 2024 10-K (SEC filing, PDF, Feb 2025) — capacity table p.9, retail p.12
- PBF 2024 10-K (SEC filing, PDF, Feb 2025) — refineries pp.10-12, NCI table p.11
- PSX 2024 10-K (SEC filing, HTML, Feb 2025)
- DINO 2024 earnings release (Feb 2025) — capacity 678 BPSD
- Reliance Integrated Annual Report 2023-24 (PDF) — O2C revenue p.50
- Reliance O2C FY2024-25 (web page, Apr 2025)
- S-Oil investor relations (web) — revenue/operating income tables
- Sinopec 2024 Annual Results Announcement (web, Mar 2025)
- Various Wikipedia, Statista, Reuters for supplementary capacity benchmarks

Q1.rationale: Several capacity figures were directionally close, but the answer often used FY2024/nameplate data and missed required FY2025 restatement or event flags. PSX and Sinopec had material consolidation/reconciliation errors.

Q2.rationale: PBF was largely correct, and Reliance/S-Oil single-site concentration was recognized. Most HHIs, vintage cohorts, and the diversification ranking were materially wrong, especially Sinopec and HF Sinclair.

Q3.rationale: US revenue figures were often roughly in range but lacked precise eliminations, citations, or correct per-barrel denominators. Reliance lacked a proper refining carve-out, and S-Oil/Sinopec missed key dual-FX and gross-vs-external treatment.

Q4.rationale: The answer used mostly wrong fiscal-year EBITDA/margin anchors and did not provide the required four-component decompositions. Counterfactual EBITDA was incomplete and mis-benchmarked.

Q5.rationale: Some system NCI values were directionally plausible, but per-refinery inputs, disclosure years, and ND methodologies were mostly absent or weak. Complexity-adjusted margins were driven by incorrect Q4 margins and rankings were wrong.

Q6.rationale: Some utilization estimates were near plausible ranges, but denominators and FY2025 bases were inconsistent. Required downtime decomposition was largely missing, including PBF Martinez, PSX structural changes, and Sinopec economic run-cuts.

Q7.rationale: PBF's no-retail status was recognized, and some total station counts were directionally close. Tier splits, integration ratios, and the integration-depth ranking were often wrong, with major errors for PSX, S-Oil, Sinopec, and Reliance.

Q8.rationale: Most Scope 1 figures were materially wrong and often confused refining-only, O2C/group, equity-share, and operational-control bases. The answer also misidentified the highest and lowest intensity operators.

**Clean Cash Margin derivation:**
- US GAAP LIFO filers (MPC, VLO, PSX, DINO): Clean margin = EBITDA/bbl − inventory effect (LIFO reserve change). LIFO reserve increases in rising-price environments create paper EBITDA boosts that are non-cash.
- IFRS/FIFO filers (PBF, RIL, S-Oil, Sinopec): No LIFO effect, but FIFO can create headwinds when crude prices fall (older, cheaper inventory flows through COGS, inflating margin artificially). Reverse this adjustment.

| 6 | **RIL** | **21.1** | Jamnagar SEZ: 21.1; Jamnagar DTA: ~20.0 | Reliance business page (ril.com); company disclosures | 2024 | $7.0 | **$0.33** | 8 |
| 7 | **S-Oil** | **~12.0** | Ulsan CDU1: 11.0, CDU2: 12.5, CDU3: 12.5 | S-Oil ESG Report 2024; third-party database (Ametheus/OGJ); S-Oil operates as a single integrated complex | 2024 | $10.5 | **$0.88** | 2 |
| 8 | **Sinopec** | **~8.5** (estimated) | Zhenhai 11.0, Maoming 9.5, Yangzi 10.0, Yanshan 8.0, others 6–9 | Regulator filings (China NDRC); OGJ World Refinery Survey; third-party databases | 2023–2024 | $5.0 | **$0.59** | 5 |

**EBITDA per Complexity-Bbl ranking:**
1. **S-Oil** ($0.88) — Single-site, high NCI, strong Asian product cracks
2. **MPC** ($0.68) — Largest US refiner, strong Gulf Coast positioning
3. **Sinopec** ($0.59) — Scale advantages, lower NCI but high absolute EBITDA
4. **VLO** ($0.55) — High NCI but lower crack capture in 2024
5. **PSX** ($0.45)
6. **RIL** ($0.33)
7. **PBF** ($0.35)
8. **DINO** ($0.32)

**Methodology note for Asian filers:** Reliance NCI of 21.1 is company-disclosed (ril.com business page). S-Oil NCI is derived from OGJ World Refinery Survey data and company ESG report descriptions of upgrading units. Sinopec NCI is estimated from China NDRC refinery registry data and OGJ survey averages, as Sinopec does not publish per-refinery NCI.

---

## Q6. Utilization Rate — Reverse-Engineered & Downtime Decomposition

| # | Entity | Actual Throughput (kbd) | Operable Capacity (kbd) | Utilization % | Planned Turnaround | Unplanned Outage | Economic Run-Cuts | Data Availability |
|---|--------|------------------------|------------------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------|--------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **MPC** | ~2,680 | 2,963 | **90.5%** | Disclosed: heavy maintenance in H1 2024 | Not separately quantified | Q4 2024: ~88% run rate | 10-K provides utilization guidance |
| 2 | **VLO** | ~2,800 | 3,000–3,200 | **89–93%** | Q3 2024 planned at 92% of capacity | Not separately disclosed | Q1 2026: ~92% | Quarterly earnings releases |
| 3 | **PSX** | ~1,650 | 1,800 | **91.7%** | San Francisco conversion took capacity offline | Not separately disclosed | Low-mid 90% range per Reuters | 10-K + earnings calls |

| 5 | **PBF** | ~850 | 1,000 | **85.0%** | Extensive turnaround work in 2024 (all refineries) | Martinez underperformance | Economic run-cuts at Martinez | Earnings release notes |
| 6 | **RIL** | ~1,350 | 1,400 | **96.4%** | Not separately disclosed (Indian regulator filings may have details) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Throughput from production meant for sale; utilization reverse-engineered |

| 8 | **Sinopec** | ~5,050 | ~5,500–6,000 | **84–92%** | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | 2024 throughput down 2% YoY (Reuters) — likely economic run-cuts | Throughput from annual results announcement |

**Note:** US refiners generally disclose utilization in quarterly earnings releases. Asian filers (RIL, S-Oil, Sinopec) typically do not report utilization percentages directly; reverse-engineered from throughput ÷ capacity. Turnaround/unplanned/economic split is generally **not disclosed** by Asian filers in English-language reports.

## Q7. Retail Footprint — Tiered Decomposition & Integration Depth

| # | Entity | Total Branded Sites | Company-Operated | Dealer/Lessee | Jobber/Wholesale | Franchised | Integration Ratio (kbd per 1,000 stations) | Throughput/Station (bbl/day) |
|---|--------|--------------------|------------------|---------------|------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
